clue.text: Quick chat with GP about keeping one's head

indicators.note: keeping means the combined letters hold the next piece within them
about here turns the doctor round so it reads backwards

parts.note: a GP (general practitioner) is a doctor, abbreviated DR

indicators.note: head points to the opening letter of one's

parts.note: its first letter supplies the piece kept inside

explanation.surface: A patient wants a brief chat with their family doctor about staying calm under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: W plus DR turned round ('about') gives WRD, which keeps O, the head of 'one's', inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a quick talk with someone is a common idiom for a brief conversation, so the noun stands for it.

clue.text: Opposed to admitting disorderly bar element

indicators.note: admitting means letting the next piece in, so it sits inside

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: disorderly signals that the letters of bar are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone objects to letting an unruly pub into the neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: CON takes in ARB, the letters of 'bar' rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Carbon is a chemical element, number six in the periodic table, so it is an example of the category.

clue.text: So there you may see shifts as busy cook

indicators.note: shifts means the letters of as busy cook move around into a new order

explanation.surface: A cook who works busy shifts might say a defiant 'So there!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'you may see' is only a link between the definition and the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are childish exclamations of defiance or triumph, said to taunt someone who has lost an argument.

clue.text: To come off worse, let in 400

definitions.note: used as an adverb, as in 'push the door to', meaning shut

indicators.note: let in means the second piece is admitted inside the first

parts.note: CD is 400 in Roman numerals
to come off worse in a contest is to lose

explanation.surface: It reads as a sporting team being beaten after conceding 400 runs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To' looks like a mere link word but it is the definition: a door pushed to is closed.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb to, as in pulling a door to, means into a shut position, which is what the answer describes.

clue.text: Stunning punch from below fair? Nose bust in two places

indicators.note: in a down clue, read from below means these letters are read upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: OK means fair, satisfactory
conk is slang for the nose

indicators.note: bust is broken in two places, losing two of its letters and leaving the middle pair

explanation.surface: A boxer's uppercut busts an opponent's nose twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: OK and CONK read from below give KNOCKO; 'bust' broken in two places loses B and S, leaving UT to finish the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A knockout is a blow that leaves the opponent unconscious and ends the boxing bout.

clue.text: Two homophones for "cut" and "fruit"

indicators.note: homophones for says the answer sounds the same as the words for these things

parts.note: to pare is to cut or trim, and a pear is a fruit; both are pronounced like the answer

explanation.surface: It reads as a grammar exercise asking for sound-alike words.
explanation.walkthrough: PARE (cut) and PEAR (fruit) both sound just like the answer, so either gives it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair is a set of two things, so the number word stands for a couple.

clue.text: Team members breaking the same shot record

parts.note: DO is the abbreviation of ditto, meaning the same

indicators.note: breaking means the team members go into the middle of the shot

parts.note: a cut is a shot in cricket
men are members of a team

explanation.surface: Players bettering the same shot to set a new record.
explanation.walkthrough: DO (ditto) is followed by CUT with MEN breaking into it; in cricket a cut is a shot played square of the wicket.
explanation.definitionFit: A document is a written record, so the noun is a synonym for an official account kept on paper.

clue.text: People sampling leaves dug daisies?

parts.note: a dug is an udder or teat
asters are daisy-like flowers of the family Asteraceae

explanation.surface: It asks whether a dug-up bed of daisies is the work of samplers of leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dug' looks like a verb but is the noun for an animal's teat.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea tasters are professionals who sample and grade tea, and tea comes as dried leaves.

clue.text: Who's made most prominent of offices by degrees?

definitions.text: Who's made most prominent of offices by degrees?
definitions.note: describes a man who reached the top office, the US presidency

indicators.note: the most prominent letter of a word is taken as its leading one

parts.note: BA and MA are the Bachelor of Arts and Master of Arts degrees

explanation.surface: Who rose step by step to the most prominent office of all?
explanation.walkthrough: O, the first of 'offices', plus two degrees, BA and MA; the whole clue also describes the former US president, a Harvard-trained lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: Barack Obama rose to the American presidency, the most powerful post, after Columbia and Harvard degrees.

clue.text: Canary Yellow fanzine periodically on the counter, delayed in circulation?

indicators.note: in circulation means going around the reversed piece, enclosing it

parts.note: delayed means late

indicators.note: on the counter suggests running anticlockwise, i.e. backwards

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold or yellow

indicators.note: periodically means taking letters at regular intervals, every other one

parts.note: its even letters give the piece

explanation.surface: A canary-yellow fan magazine sits on a shop counter, its issue late in circulation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canary' looks like the bird or the colour but means one of the Canary Islands. Or is heraldry's yellow; 'periodically' takes the even letters of fanzine.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanzarote is one of the Canary Islands, Spanish territory off the north-west coast of Africa.

clue.text: In ceremony, call notes of credit "iffy" …

parts.note: to dub is to confer a title in a ceremony, as when tapping a knight with a sword
IOUs are notes acknowledging a debt

explanation.surface: A formal occasion where someone's notes of credit are deemed questionable.
explanation.walkthrough: To dub someone a knight is to call them Sir in a ceremony; that leads straight into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Iffy is colloquial for doubtful or questionable, the same sense as the answer.

clue.text: … after which, did you hear Hoy maybe do one in honour?

indicators.note: did you hear signals that the answer is spoken like the words before it

parts.note: Sir Chris Hoy, knighted Olympic cyclist; Kit is a pet form of Christopher, so he might be Sir Kit

explanation.surface: After his knighthood, would the cyclist Chris Hoy ride a celebratory lap?
explanation.walkthrough: 'after which' points back to the dubbing in the previous clue: once knighted, Chris Hoy is Sir Chris, and Chris could be Kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A lap of honour is a single circuit of the track made in celebration, so a circuit is one lap.

clue.text: Rubbish hill-workers deposited at back of tip

indicators.note: deposited at says the workers are placed against that letter, following it
back of points to the last letter of the word tip

parts.note: its final letter is the piece
ants are workers that build anthills

explanation.surface: Rubbish dumped by labourers at the back of a refuse tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hill-workers' suggests miners or farmhands, but they are ants from an anthill.
explanation.definitionFit: Pants is British slang for something worthless or of poor quality, a synonym for rubbish.

clue.text: Wire mark on skin doing what scab does?

indicators.note: doing what a scab does means crossing, i.e. going through the picket, so the mark goes inside it

parts.note: a scab (strikebreaker) crosses a picket, so the picket is what the action involves
a pock is a pit or scar left on the skin

explanation.surface: It sounds like a medical question about a skin mark and how a scab forms.
explanation.walkthrough: A scab here is a strikebreaker, not a crust on a wound: a scab crosses the PICKET line, so POCK crosses into PICKET. Wire is old slang for a pickpocket.
explanation.definitionFit: In old thieves' slang a wire was a pickpocket, from the hooked wire once used to lift purses.

clue.text: It's odd, on reflection, Lord North's not so grasping

definitions.note: the answer is a quality, so it names what something odd has

indicators.note: on reflection means the word Lord is seen as in a mirror, backwards
grasping means holding the North abbreviation within

parts.note: less means not so, as in less keen

explanation.surface: It reads like a comment on the Prime Minister Lord North being less greedy than usual.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord North was British Prime Minister during the American War of Independence; here he is just LORD reversed and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Drollness is quaint or whimsical humour, the quality of being amusingly odd.

clue.text: It's not all fruit juice loading on the wagon — what's in keg?

definitions.note: said of the perfect word: 'it's exactly it'

indicators.note: not all means the fruit is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a lemon is a fruit

indicators.note: loading means the juice is packed inside the teetotal letters

parts.note: TT stands for teetotal, which is what someone on the wagon is
jus is juice, as in a meat jus

indicators.note: what's in points to the inner letter of keg

parts.note: its middle letter is the piece

explanation.surface: A teetotaller on the wagon remarks that the keg holds more than just fruit juice.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the exclamation 'It's!', the cry when the exact phrase is found. Jus is the French for juice, used in cooking; TT is teetotal.
explanation.definitionFit: Le mot juste is the precisely right expression, the one about which you would say 'that's it'.

clue.text: Fresh but eccentric crossword compiler repeatedly pumps up the volume

indicators.note: pumps up means the setter's letters are pumped into the middle of the jumble
fresh means the letters of but eccentric are made anew in a different order

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as I and then again as ME

explanation.surface: An eccentric crossword setter turns up the music.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of 'but eccentric' has I and ME pumped into it; the setter is both I and ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A cubic centimetre is a unit for measuring volume, a millilitre's worth of space.

clue.text: Red part of Manchester belting Arsenal, with number 4 coming off Odegaard's butt

indicators.note: belting means wrapping around, like a belt around the middle

parts.note: Bury is a town in Greater Manchester

indicators.note: number 4 coming off means the fourth letter of the weapons is removed

parts.note: an arsenal holds guns; Arsenal football club are also the Gunners
D is the last letter, the butt end, of the name Odegaard

explanation.surface: A football story: Manchester players beating Arsenal while Odegaard, Arsenal's captain, is substituted.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal is the London football club, but here an arsenal is a store of weapons. Bury is a town in Greater Manchester; 'number 4' is the fourth letter of the weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Burgundy is both a red wine from that French region and the dark purplish-red colour named after it.

clue.text: Was ringer once given a eulogy?

parts.note: ex means former, once
a bell that tolled was ringing, as a ringer does

explanation.surface: It asks whether a former bell-ringer received a tribute.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it EX-TOLLED: once having tolled, as a bell-ringer would.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise lavishly, so someone extolled has received high praise such as a eulogy.

clue.text: I confirm you will be charged over constant scrounging

indicators.note: over means the phrase is turned over, read in reverse

parts.words: I confirm you will be charged
parts.note: a police officer might say 'it is a rap', confirming the charge will stick
c is the constant for the speed of light

explanation.surface: A policeman confirms a charge over a constant habit of scrounging.
explanation.walkthrough: IT IS A RAP turned over gives PARASITI, then C, the physics constant for the speed of light.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasite lives off others, so parasitic behaviour is sponging or freeloading.

clue.text: Number 2022? Down?

parts.note: to number is to count
2022 is a year, abbreviated Y

explanation.surface: A cryptic-looking query about a number and a year, followed by a direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down' looks like the clue's direction or a mood, but it is County Down in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Down is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland, so it is an example of the category.

clue.text: Credit store's spring cut is operating like clockwork

indicators.note: cut means the spring word is removed from the credit store

parts.note: a tick shop sells goods on tick, i.e. on credit
to hop is to spring or jump

explanation.surface: A shop's spring sale running smoothly.
explanation.walkthrough: On tick is British slang for on credit, so a tick shop is a credit store; 's is 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: A clock mechanism ticks as it runs, so something that ticks is functioning like clockwork.

clue.text: Manages to suppress patient's heart issues

indicators.note: to suppress means to hold something down inside

parts.note: copes means manages

indicators.note: heart points to the central letter of the word patient

parts.note: its fourth letter, at the centre of patient, is the piece

explanation.surface: Managing to keep a patient's heart problems under control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issues' looks like problems but means copies of a publication.
explanation.definitionFit: Copies of a magazine or newspaper are its issues, the editions printed and distributed.

clue.text: Senior soldier has hooks in governors

indicators.note: in here means the hooks go inside the colonel's letters

parts.note: COL is short for colonel
unci is the plural of uncus, a hook

explanation.surface: A senior army officer keeps meat hooks in his quarters among the governors.
explanation.walkthrough: Unci is the Latin-derived plural of uncus, a hook-shaped body part.
explanation.definitionFit: A council is a governing body, so its members collectively govern a town or organisation.

clue.text: Who will stay up late to track Capone's #1 hood?

indicators.note: to track means following behind, so the bird comes after
#1 means the first letter of the gangster's name

parts.note: its first letter is the piece
a night owl stays up late

explanation.surface: A late-night watcher tails gangster Al Capone's top hoodlum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hood' looks like a gangster, fitting Capone, but it is a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowl is a loose hood, especially one attached to a monk's habit.

clue.text: Penny Shylock's taken — by force, I assume

indicators.note: taken means the moneylender has taken the penny in

parts.note: Shylock, the moneylender in The Merchant of Venice, gives his name to a usurer

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's moneylender takes a penny by force.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks in the answer's own voice: one who seizes a throne says 'I assume power by force'.
explanation.definitionFit: A usurper takes a position or power illegally or by force, assuming a role not rightfully theirs.

clue.text: Pity old book was about her

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an old word for pity or compassion
second meaning: an Old Testament book is named after the Moabite woman whose story it tells

explanation.walkthrough: 'old book' points to the Old Testament, where one book is named after the woman it describes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruth survives in ruthless as the old noun for compassion, and she is the Moabite heroine of a biblical book.

clue.text: Before he's quit The Archers, Bert's first made final provision

indicators.note: before means the archers come ahead of what remains of The
made means that letter is turned into the word for final

parts.note: bowmen are archers

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of Bert

parts.note: its first letter is the one swapped
end means the final part

indicators.note: quit means he leaves the word The, leaving a single letter

parts.note: he is the word taken away

explanation.surface: A radio story: before leaving The Archers, the character Bert made final provision in his will.
explanation.walkthrough: The Archers is a long-running BBC radio soap; here it is just bowmen. BOWMEN with B made END gives ENDOWMEN, then T from The without he.
explanation.definitionFit: An endowment is money provided to fund an institution or person, a lasting provision of income.

clue.text: Newspaper plagiarism?

parts.note: read as a paper's name split 3,1,1 (the Financial Times with its article), it also describes stealing someone's words

explanation.walkthrough: Split it THE FT: the Financial Times, Britain's pink business daily; joined up it is stealing, which plagiarism is.
explanation.definitionFit: Plagiarism is stealing someone else's words or ideas, a form of intellectual stealing that a paper could commit.
